stem: 'Universal adult franchise' means that:
options: Every adult citizen has the right to vote
solution: Universal adult franchise gives every adult citizen the right to vote, regardless of caste, religion, gender, education or wealth.

stem: In India, the minimum age to vote is:
solution: Every Indian citizen aged 18 years and above has the right to vote.

stem: The voting age in India was lowered from 21 to 18 years by which constitutional amendment?
solution: The 61st Constitutional Amendment (1988) lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years.

stem: Elections in India are conducted by the:
solution: The Election Commission of India, an independent constitutional body, conducts and supervises elections.

stem: The Election Commission of India is provided for under which Article of the Constitution?
solution: Article 324 of the Constitution provides for the Election Commission, which superintends and conducts elections.

stem: India's first general elections were held in:
solution: India's first general elections to the Lok Sabha were held in 1951-52.

stem: The first Chief Election Commissioner of India was:
solution: Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India, who oversaw the first general elections.

stem: The principle 'one person, one vote, one value' means that:
options: Every voter has one vote of equal worth
solution: 'One person, one vote, one value' ensures that every voter has exactly one vote and that all votes carry equal weight.

stem: Voting in Indian elections is done through a:
solution: Elections use the secret ballot, so a voter's choice remains private and free from pressure.

stem: The electronic device now used to record votes in Indian elections is the:
solution: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) are used to record and count votes in Indian elections.

stem: The area from which a candidate is elected is called a:
solution: A constituency is the geographical area whose voters elect one representative.

stem: The official list of all eligible voters in a constituency is called the:
solution: The electoral roll (voters' list) contains the names of all citizens eligible to vote in a constituency.

stem: Some constituencies are 'reserved' for candidates from:
solution: Certain constituencies are reserved for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe candidates to ensure their representation.

stem: The Indian electoral system generally follows the __________ method, in which the candidate with the most votes wins.
solution: India mainly uses the first-past-the-post system: the candidate who gets the most votes in a constituency wins that seat.

stem: Universal adult franchise is important because it makes the government:
solution: By giving every adult an equal vote, universal franchise makes the government answerable to all citizens, upholding political equality.

stem: The 'Model Code of Conduct' is a set of guidelines that:
options: Political parties and candidates must follow during elections
solution: The Model Code of Conduct lays down rules of behaviour for parties and candidates during elections to ensure they are free and fair.

stem: The right to vote regardless of caste, religion, gender or wealth reflects the value of:
solution: Universal adult franchise reflects political equality — the idea that all citizens have an equal say in choosing their government.

stem: Elections held to fill a seat that falls vacant between general elections are called:
solution: A by-election is held to fill a single seat that becomes vacant (e.g. due to death or resignation) between general elections.

stem: The independence of the Election Commission is important so that elections are:
options: Free, fair and not influenced by the ruling party
solution: An independent Election Commission ensures elections are free and fair and not manipulated by the party in power.

stem: The option on the ballot/EVM that lets a voter reject all candidates is called:
solution: NOTA ('None Of The Above') allows a voter to formally reject all the candidates contesting in a constituency.

stem: Universal franchise was a bold step in India because it was granted:
options: To all adults from the very beginning, despite widespread poverty and illiteracy
Only to the literate at first
solution: India granted universal adult franchise to all adults from the very start, a remarkable step given the widespread poverty and illiteracy of the time.

stem: The purpose of holding regular elections is to:
options: Let citizens choose and change their representatives peacefully
solution: Regular elections allow citizens to choose their representatives and to peacefully change the government if they wish.

stem: A voter's choice being kept secret helps to ensure that:
options: People can vote freely without fear or pressure
solution: The secret ballot protects voters from intimidation and pressure, allowing them to vote according to their own free choice.

stem: The division of the country into constituencies of roughly equal population is done through:
solution: Delimitation is the process of drawing the boundaries of constituencies so that each has roughly equal population.

stem: Which document/card is commonly used to identify a voter at the polling booth?
options: The Voter ID (Electoral Photo Identity Card)
solution: The Voter ID (EPIC) issued by the Election Commission is commonly used to identify voters, though other approved IDs may also be accepted.

stem: Universal adult franchise strengthens democracy by ensuring that:
options: Every citizen, however poor, has a say in governance
solution: By giving every adult a vote, universal franchise ensures that even the poorest citizen has a say in choosing the government.

stem: Reserved constituencies were created to:
options: Ensure representation of historically disadvantaged groups (SCs and STs)
Give more seats to the rich
solution: Reserved constituencies ensure that Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes are represented in legislatures, correcting historical disadvantage.

stem: The counting of votes and declaration of results is supervised by the:
solution: The Election Commission supervises the counting of votes and the declaration of results to ensure fairness.

stem: The first-past-the-post system means the winner is the candidate who:
options: Gets more votes than any other candidate in the constituency
Gets more than half of all votes only
solution: Under first-past-the-post, the candidate with the highest number of votes in a constituency wins, even without an absolute majority.

stem: Free and fair elections require that:
options: Everyone can vote freely and votes are counted honestly
Only the ruling party can campaign
The results are decided in advance
solution: Free and fair elections require universal franchise, secret voting, honest counting and an even playing field for all parties.

stem: The main reason universal franchise is linked to equality is that:
options: It gives every citizen an equal vote, regardless of status
solution: Universal franchise embodies equality by granting every citizen a single, equally-weighted vote irrespective of their status.

stem: The people who contest elections to become representatives are called:
solution: Candidates are the persons who stand for election, seeking to be chosen by voters as their representatives.

stem: A political party that wins a majority of seats in the Lok Sabha usually:
solution: The party (or coalition) that wins a majority of seats forms the government.

stem: Which of the following is essential for the electoral system to be democratic?
options: Equal voting rights and an independent election authority
Control of elections by the ruling party
solution: A democratic electoral system requires equal voting rights (universal franchise) and an independent authority to conduct fair elections.

stem: The right to vote is a form of:
solution: Voting is a key form of political participation through which citizens take part in choosing their government.

stem: Election campaigns allow parties and candidates to:
options: Present their programmes and win the support of voters
solution: During campaigns, parties and candidates present their policies and programmes to win the voters' support.

stem: The value of universal franchise is that it treats:
options: The vote of a poor person as equal to that of a rich person
solution: Universal franchise treats every vote as equal — a poor person's vote counts exactly as much as a rich person's.

stem: Which of the following can lead to disqualification of a candidate or malpractice in elections?
options: Bribing voters or using unfair means
Following the Model Code of Conduct
solution: Bribing voters, intimidation and other unfair means are electoral malpractices that are prohibited and punishable.

stem: The introduction of EVMs has helped make the voting process:
options: Faster and easier to count, with fewer invalid votes
solution: EVMs make voting simpler, speed up counting and reduce the number of invalid votes compared with paper ballots.

stem: In a democracy, the ultimate power to choose the government rests with the:
solution: In a democracy, the people, through their votes, hold the ultimate power to choose and change the government.

stem: The idea that all adults should vote, even the poor and illiterate, was based on the belief that:
options: Every citizen is capable of choosing their representatives
solution: Universal franchise rests on the belief that every adult citizen is capable of, and entitled to, a say in choosing the government.

stem: The Election Commission ensures a level playing field by enforcing the:
options: Model Code of Conduct on all parties
solution: By enforcing the Model Code of Conduct equally on all parties, the Election Commission ensures a level playing field.

stem: The success of Indian democracy owes much to its:
options: Commitment to universal adult franchise and regular free elections
solution: India's democracy has been sustained by its commitment to universal adult franchise and to holding regular, free and fair elections.

stem: A key difference between universal franchise and restricted franchise is that universal franchise:
options: Extends the vote to all adults, not just a privileged few
solution: Universal franchise gives the vote to all adult citizens, unlike restricted franchise which limits it to a privileged group.

stem: Which of the following statements about India's electoral system is correct?
options: It is based on universal adult franchise and conducted by an independent Election Commission
Elections are run by the ruling party
solution: India's electoral system rests on universal adult franchise and is conducted by an independent Election Commission through secret ballot.

stem: The freedom of voters to choose without fear is protected by:
options: The secret ballot and the Model Code of Conduct
solution: The secret ballot and rules like the Model Code of Conduct protect voters' freedom to choose without fear or pressure.

stem: The extension of the vote to women along with men from the start reflects India's commitment to:
solution: Granting women the vote from the outset, along with men, reflects India's commitment to gender equality in political rights.

stem: Political parties are important in the electoral system because they:
options: Contest elections, form governments and offer policy choices to voters
solution: Political parties contest elections, form governments or oppositions, and present policy choices to the voters.

stem: The right to vote is described as a great equaliser because:
options: It gives everyone an equal role in choosing the government
solution: The vote is a great equaliser because it gives every citizen, rich or poor, an equal role in choosing the government.

stem: Universal adult franchise is guaranteed by which Article of the Constitution?
solution: UNIVERSAL ADULT FRANCHISE is guaranteed by ARTICLE 326. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Election Commission of India is provided for under which Article?
solution: The ELECTION COMMISSION is provided for under ARTICLE 324. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The voting age in India was lowered from 21 to 18 years by which amendment?
solution: The VOTING AGE was lowered from 21 to 18 by the 61st AMENDMENT (1988). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The NOTA option on the EVM allows a voter to:
options: Reject all candidates ('None Of The Above')
solution: NOTA ('NONE Of The Above') allows a voter to REJECT ALL candidates. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The VVPAT machine attached to EVMs allows voters to:
options: Verify that their vote was cast for the intended candidate via a printed slip
solution: VVPAT (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail) lets voters VERIFY their vote via a PRINTED SLIP. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The card commonly used to identify a voter at the polling booth is the:
solution: The VOTER ID card (EPIC — Electoral Photo Identity Card) is commonly used to identify voters. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Election Commission of India is a ______ body (in terms of members).
options: Multi-member (Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners)
solution: The ELECTION COMMISSION is currently a MULTI-MEMBER body — the CEC and two Election Commissioners. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The minimum age to vote in India is:
solution: The minimum VOTING AGE is 18 YEARS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): Universal adult franchise was a bold step for India in 1950. Reason (R): India adopted it despite widespread poverty and illiteracy, trusting all adults equally with the vote. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — universal franchise was bold. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: India adopted it DESPITE POVERTY and ILLITERACY, TRUSTING ALL adults EQUALLY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The principle 'one person, one vote, one value' means:
options: Each voter has exactly one vote of equal worth
solution: 'ONE PERSON, ONE VOTE, ONE VALUE' means each voter has EXACTLY ONE vote of EQUAL WORTH. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The area from which a candidate is elected to the Lok Sabha is called a:
solution: The area from which a candidate is elected is a CONSTITUENCY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Indian electoral system for the Lok Sabha generally follows the:
solution: The LOK SABHA follows the FIRST-PAST-THE-POST system. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the first-past-the-post system, the winner is the candidate who:
options: Gets the most votes in the constituency
Gets more than half the total national votes
solution: In FIRST-PAST-THE-POST, the winner is the candidate with the MOST VOTES in the constituency. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The secrecy of the ballot helps ensure that:
options: Voters can vote freely without fear or pressure
Everyone knows who voted for whom
solution: The SECRET BALLOT ensures voters can vote FREELY WITHOUT FEAR or pressure. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The independence of the Election Commission is important because it:
options: Ensures elections are free, fair and impartial
solution: The INDEPENDENCE of the EC ensures elections are FREE, FAIR, and IMPARTIAL. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Universal franchise is described as a 'great equaliser' because it:
options: Gives every adult an equal say, whether rich or poor
solution: Universal franchise is a GREAT EQUALISER — it gives EVERY adult an EQUAL SAY, rich or poor. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following can lead to disqualification of a voter or candidate?
options: Certain legal grounds like being of unsound mind or convicted of specified offences
solution: DISQUALIFICATION can arise from LEGAL grounds like being of UNSOUND MIND or CONVICTED of specified offences — not poverty, gender, or lack of education. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The introduction of EVMs has helped make voting:
options: Faster, easier to count, and less prone to certain malpractices
solution: EVMs made voting FASTER, easier to COUNT, and LESS PRONE to certain malpractices. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The extension of the vote to women along with men from the very start made India:
options: A pioneer in granting universal franchise regardless of gender
solution: By extending the VOTE to WOMEN and men from the START, India was a PIONEER in universal franchise regardless of GENDER. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Election Commission ensures a level playing field by:
options: Enforcing the Model Code of Conduct and monitoring campaigns
solution: The EC ensures a LEVEL PLAYING FIELD by ENFORCING the MODEL CODE of CONDUCT and MONITORING campaigns. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A key difference between universal franchise and restricted franchise is that restricted franchise:
options: Limited voting to certain groups (e.g., propertied men)
solution: RESTRICTED FRANCHISE LIMITED voting to certain groups (e.g., PROPERTIED MEN), unlike universal franchise. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The division of the country into constituencies of roughly equal population is done to:
options: Ensure each vote has roughly equal weight
solution: DIVIDING into constituencies of roughly EQUAL POPULATION ensures each VOTE has roughly EQUAL WEIGHT. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The process of redrawing constituency boundaries based on population is called:
solution: Redrawing constituency boundaries based on POPULATION is DELIMITATION. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the pairs: 1. Article 324 — Election Commission 2. Article 326 — universal adult franchise 3. NOTA — reject all candidates. How many are correctly matched?
solution: ALL THREE match: ARTICLE 324 → Election Commission; ARTICLE 326 → universal adult franchise; NOTA → reject all candidates. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A political party that wins a majority of seats in the Lok Sabha:
solution: A party winning a MAJORITY of seats FORMS the GOVERNMENT. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall message of 'Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System' is that:
options: Every adult's equal right to vote, exercised through free and fair elections, is the foundation of Indian democracy
Voting should be limited to a few
Only the rich should choose the government
solution: The chapter explains how universal adult franchise and free, fair elections form the foundation of Indian democracy.
